The method is evaluated on wheat crops both in silico (i.e. simulations based on the AdelWheat functional structural crop model coupled with a point cloud simulator) and in actual phenotyping trials of a panel of 10 bread wheat genotypes grown in two study sites under different treatments of plant density, water stress and sowing dates. The in silico validation indicates that the numeric inversion of BL with the LiDAR system of the Phenomobile leads to a relative error of 9.8% (RMSE = 0.32, R 2 = 0.99) and 8.4% (RMSE =5.4°, R 2 = 0.95) in the estimation of PAI and AIA , respectively. The validation in actual phenotyping experiments against destructive measurements produced satisfactory results for canopy PAI (RMSE = 1.44, R 2 = 0.82), while requiring prior knowledge on AIA , e.g. either by (i) introducing a regularization term in the cost function used to invert BL, to avoid unexpected high AIA estimations, (ii) using a fixed, reference value of 60°. The analysis of the results indicates that the inclusion of a regularization term mitigates the impact of actual differences in leaf inclination among cultivars on PAI accuracy, while providing a relative description of the actual variability in the vertical profile of leaf inclination across the different cultivars.

title: Towards continental-scale SWOT-based modeling of reservoir operations
summary: The advent of reservoir models has enabled the monitoring and prediction of reservoir operations (inflow, storage, and release); however, the in situ operation data used for model parameterization is spatially scarce. In this study, we evaluate reservoir monitoring capabilities by leveraging observations from multiple satellite missions to reconstruct reservoir operations, optimize reservoir model parameters, and simulate operations. For reservoirs in the US and Brazil, we design a set of experiments relying on different combinations of in situ , satellite, and hydrologically modeled data sources as reservoir model inputs to characterize the error of satellite- and model-informed reservoir operations. We also make the first attempt to evaluate the use of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite mission data record for reservoir optimization and simulation. Our results show that simulated storages (median nRMSE ≤ 0.30–0.50; represents maximum across experiments for each country and altimetry dataset) perform significantly better across all experiments than simulated releases (median nRMSE ≤ 0.68–0.94). Accuracy of simulated releases is strongly dependent on the quality of the inflow time series: using in situ inflow (median KGE = 0.56–0.68) for reservoir modeling has greater accuracy than hydrologically modeled inflow (median KGE = −0.19–0.15). However, when simulating operations based on altimetry and modeled inflow, 42–67% of reservoirs improve in release KGE compared to simulations without reservoir operations. Overall, our study demonstrates the potential of SWOT and other satellite altimeters for continental-scale reservoir storage monitoring, and that improving inflow simulations is crucial for release monitoring.

title: Estimation of rice leaf angle distribution from geometric features in millimetric-resolution UAV RGB imagery acquired at 45° viewing angle
summary: No abstract available in OpenAlex.

title: A novel framework for urban–rural gradient classification by integrating multidimensional urbanization features via self-supervised learning
summary: Rapid urbanization has transformed vast natural landscapes into increasingly complex human-dominated environments, giving rise to pronounced urban–rural gradients. However, accurate classification of such gradients remains challenging because biophysical indicators alone cannot fully represent the socioeconomic heterogeneity embedded in the urban–rural continuum. Here, based on multisource Earth observation and geospatial datasets, we propose a novel urban–rural gradient classification framework that integrates multidimensional urbanization features, including, land development, population density, economic intensity, and social vitality, to establish a five-class urban–rural gradient classification scheme-Urban core, Urban area, Suburban area, Rural area, and Natural area. Then, we developed URGCNet, a spatial clustering-driven self-supervised learning model that incorporates ordinal constraints to capture the ordered structure of the urban–rural continuum. Based on this framework, we produced URGCdataset, a 500 m urban–rural gradient classification dataset for mainland China for five benchmark years (2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025). The framework achieved strong classification performance, with URGCNet reaching an overall accuracy of 91.0% and URGCdataset reaching 93.6% against an independent test sample dataset. Ablation experiments show that removing individual urbanization features reduced the Kappa coefficient by 0.1–0.2, highlighting the indispensable role of socioeconomic information beyond biophysical indicators. Spatiotemporal analysis reveals a clear expansion of human-activity areas over the 2005–2025 period, during which the share of natural areas decreased from 92.7% to 90.0%. Overall, this framework provides a transferable pathway for establishing comparable urban–rural gradient classifications across diverse regional contexts and offers a new spatial foundation for urban environmental and ecological applications.

title: Detection of soil moisture variations beneath an asphalt layer using L-band SAR
summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)-based soil moisture retrieval has primarily focused on bare or vegetated surfaces, whereas asphalt generally considered a highly attenuating medium that limits the detection of subsurface soil. Here, we used an L-band SAR sensor in a microwave anechoic chamber to characterize the detectable depth through asphalt and its controlling factors, and further quantitatively investigate the responses of interferometric phase, coherence, and closure phase to infiltration-induced variations in subsurface soil moisture. Results show subsurface echoes remain detectable through at least 9 cm of asphalt using an L-band Mini-SAR, while modeling indicates that increasing transmit power and antenna aperture could extend detectable depth beyond 30 cm. The InSAR observables exhibited distinct responses to infiltration-induced subsurface moisture variations. The mean interferometric phase decreased linearly with increasing soil volumetric water content (VWC) ( r = - 0.992 ), with an average phase shift of approximately 0.53° per 1 % increase in VWC. Spatial analysis further revealed a strong correspondence between regions of reduced coherence and nonzero closure phase and the infiltration-affected area. Overall, this study provides theoretical and methodological support for improving the subsurface detectability of airborne and vehicle-based L-band SAR sensors and for InSAR-based detection of soil moisture variations beneath asphalt layers.

title: InterMine: A foundation model-based multi-task interaction network for remote sensing interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity
summary: The interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity is critical for resource management and ecological protection. It comprises two key tasks: extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. However, existing methods usually suffer from task separation, and their outputs cannot fully meet the requirements of interpretation. Therefore, this study proposes a foundation model-based multi-task interaction network (InterMine) to jointly perform open-pit mine extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. First, InterMine employs a Siamese foundation model as the encoder to enhance feature representation from images of complex open-pit coal mines and incorporates a channel-spatial feature reconstruction module to adapt the encoded features to meet the semantic and spatial requirements of the decoder. Second, a multi-task interaction mechanism is proposed to facilitate complementary information exchange between tasks. Finally, a consistency loss function based on hard-sample reweighting is designed to mitigate inconsistencies among multi-task outputs. InterMine is trained and evaluated on a self-constructed multi-temporal open-pit coal mining activity interpretation dataset (OMSet). Experimental results demonstrate that InterMine outperforms the compared methods. In particular, InterMine achieves F1-scores of 87.57 %, 83.68 %, and 79.43 % for open-pit mine extent extraction, excavation change detection, and reclamation change detection, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods by 1.89 ∼ 5.29, 3.04 ∼ 7.83, and 2.79 ∼ 7.42 percentage points, respectively. This work provides both technical and data support for open-pit coal mine monitoring. OMSet and the code of InterMine have been made publicly available at https://figshare.com/s/03c029d8e4846faef69f .

title: Density-dominated aggregation and spatiotemporal differentiation of yellow sea green tides revealed by long term observations
summary: Green tides dominated by Ulva prolifera have bloomed in the Yellow Sea since 2008, posing persistent threats to coastal ecosystems. While multiple indicators (including bloom extent, pixel area, coverage area, and biomass) have been used to characterize bloom dynamics, their inconsistent use may obscure assessments of bloom intensity and spatiotemporal variability, leaving their variations across spatial perspectives poorly understood and limiting their practical utility for green tide management. Here, we investigate how the interannual dynamics of Yellow Sea green tides during 2008–2024 differ when evaluated in terms of biomass rather than bloom extent, and the spatial patterns underlying these differences. The annual biomass variability peaked at 3.6 times the long-term average, exceeding the 2.0 times observed for bloom extent. This indicates increasingly dense and aggregated U. prolifera distributions and an underestimation of interannual bloom intensity by bloom extent. In the Subei Bank Front (SBF) perspective, MODIS observations show that U. prolifera first appear near the SBF in early May. U. prolifera biomass in the northern region closely tracked annual biomass across the Yellow Sea, making it the dominant contributor to interannual bloom variability, while the southern region accounted for only 17 %. From the nearshore perspective (within 20 km of the coastline), nearshore green tide biomass has largely remained below the 2008 level (49.90 kt) over the past 16 years, except in 2015 (53.54 kt) and 2019 (70.33 kt), which exceeded it by 7 % and 41 %. The cross-validation identified the annual biomass series excluding the 20 km coastal zone and the region north of the SBF as robust proxies for annual mean biomass under data gaps, with the former yielding a substitution error of 8 %. These findings provide critical quantitative evidence for Yellow Sea green tide monitoring and sustainable coastal ecosystem management in support of SDG 14.2.

title: Fine-scale annual mapping and dynamic monitoring of shrub encroachment in alpine grasslands by integrating Sentinel-2 phenological features with Sentinel-1 structural information
summary: Shrub encroachment can alter forage resources, soil–water processes, and landscape configuration in alpine grasslands, yet annual mapping remains challenging because shrub and herbaceous canopies converge spectrally and many apparent changes occur in diffuse ecotones. We developed a 10-m annual mapping framework integrating Sentinel-2 phenology, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series information, and topographic covariates to distinguish shrubland from grassland in Maqu County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2018 to 2024. A learned SAR-derived shrubland-grassland discrimination score (SGDS) was constructed from annual Sentinel-1 descriptors using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression to improve shrubland-grassland discrimination. In the 2024 benchmark experiment, the selected random forest (RF) configuration reduced classification error by approximately 17% relative to optical-only RF. SGDS outperformed the tested conventional SAR indices and the full SAR-statistics feature set, and adding SGDS increased RF accuracy from 91.26% to 92.47%. When the selected workflow was applied independently to each mapping year, annual overall accuracies ranged from 91.6% to 95.8%, based on the same 500 temporally screened reference locations spatially separated from the model-development samples. Nominal mapped shrubland area increased from 392.3 km2 in 2018 to 648.2 km2 in 2022 before declining to 560.4 km2 in 2024. Confidence and boundary-sensitivity analyses showed that the pronounced 2020–2021 increase was largely associated with low-confidence ecotonal pixels and decreased from + 96.91 to + 6.09 km2 as the mapped-class confidence threshold increased from 0.60 to 0.80, whereas the 2022–2024 decline remained negative under all tested confidence and boundary screens. Mapped shrubland area showed an apparent positive association with annual mean temperature, but this relationship was not robust after detrending and should be considered preliminary given the seven-year record. Overall, integrating learned SAR structural information with optical phenology improved annual shrubland-grassland mapping and provided a more reliable basis for interpreting mapped dynamics, with potential for locally calibrated application in comparable alpine regions.

title: A framework for inversion and assimilation of deep-sea mirror ocean acoustic tomography observations
summary: The deep ocean plays a critical role in the global climate system. However, satellite Earth observation is limited to the sea surface, while in-situ measurements struggle to achieve synchronous coverage over vast oceanic areas. Ocean Acoustic Tomography (OAT) is an essential method for retrieving large-scale interior ocean parameters; however, its path-integral nature leads to high-dimensional and ill-posed inverse problems when applied to the deep ocean. To address this, this paper develops a unified modular framework for the inversion and assimilation of acoustic remote sensing data, specifically designed for Mirror OAT (MOAT) in the deep sea. Through a configurable dimensionality reduction representation, the framework regularizes the ill-posed inverse problem in a low-dimensional space, enabling a stable and efficient numerical solution. High-resolution ocean model-based simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate its performance. Results show that the inversion module reconstructs 3-D flow fields via a “section-to-plane” two-step method, with inversion errors below 0.15 m/s over most of the water column relative to the true fields from the high-resolution ocean model. The assimilation module integrates observations using an Ensemble Kalman Filter based on a low-dimensional subspace, improving the analysis field accuracy by approximately 35 % compared to the background field. Further sensitivity experiments indicate that the assimilation method exhibits superior robustness against observation noise, while the inversion method offers higher computational efficiency by requiring neither an ensemble of model forecasts nor sequential cycling. Parameter analyses provide a basis for selecting the appropriate approach under different scenarios. This study provides a complete workflow, from methodology to numerical validation, for efficient and accurate estimation of deep-sea interior states from MOAT observations. It may serve as a reference for the design and operational application of deep-sea 3-D remote sensing observation systems.

title: Image-projected apparent particle size distribution estimation in rock avalanches using direct deep regression from UAV imagery
summary: Due to the rapid downslope movement of fragmented rock masses, rock avalanches are among the most destructive geomorphic hazards in mountainous regions. Particle size characteristics observed at the surface provide useful information for interpreting fragmentation, transport, and depositional patterns. Recent advances in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing and deep learning have enabled novel methodologies for PSD estimation. However, achieving rapid acquisition and reliable PSD characterization under complex field conditions remains challenging. To address these challenges, we constructed and preprocessed a dedicated UAV dataset for PSD analysis from high-resolution RGB imagery acquired with a DJI Matrice 300 RTK platform. Based on this dataset, we proposed a direct deep regression pipeline to predict characteristic image-projected apparent PSD descriptors, including D 20 , D 40 , D 60 , D 80 , and D max , directly from UAV image patches. The proposed approach was compared with two baseline methods: handcrafted feature-based regression and semantic segmentation-based contour pipelines. Experimental results showed that the direct deep regression pipeline achieved better overall PSD prediction performance than the baseline approaches, with ConvNeXt-Tiny obtaining the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.23 cm and resolution-normalized MAE of 16.77 ground sampling distance (GSD) units. The model exhibited more stable predictive performance for the intermediate percentiles (D 40 –D 80 ), whereas relatively higher errors were observed for D 20 and D max . The trained model was applied to representative areas within the study deposit to generate spatial maps of surface-visible apparent PSD, demonstrating its potential for UAV-based characterization of surface particle size patterns in fragmented rock deposits. Additional transfer validation on tunnel boring machine (TBM)-excavated rock images provides preliminary evidence of cross-scenario transferability across different material and imaging conditions. True cross-event validation on independent rock avalanche deposits remains to be conducted.

title: Integrated remote sensing and geotechnical investigations of the 2022 Jiujiawan mudstone landslide in Xining city, China: from deformation monitoring to failure mechanisms
summary: Mudstone landslides are widespread worldwide, with their initiation and evolution mainly governed by the coupled effects of rock mass microstructure and hydromechanical behavior. However, the linkage between Earth observation (EO)-derived deformation signals and microscale weakening mechanisms remains poorly constrained. Using the catastrophic Jiujiawan landslide (15 September 2022, Xining, China) as a case study, this research aims to reconstruct the spatiotemporal evolution of the landslide and explain the multiscale mechanisms connecting microscale material degradation with macroscale slope failure through evidence-based interpretation. To achieve this, an integrated framework combining multisource EO data, geotechnical investigations, and laboratory analyses was applied. This approach clarifies deformation characteristics and failure mechanisms from coupled macro- and microscale perspectives. At the macroscopic scale, a high-fidelity three-dimensional model was reconstructed using unmanned aerial vehicle photogrammetry. Satellite optical imagery was used to qualitatively trace the pre-failure evolutionary trajectory, complemented by interferometric synthetic aperture radar to quantitatively reconstruct spatiotemporal displacement sequences. At the microscopic scale, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy dispersive spectroscopy characterized the mineralogical suite and microstructural fabric. These analyses reveal the properties of Paleogene mudstone intercalated with gypsum layers, showing how pore-fracture networks accelerate rock mass degradation. Synthesis of the results indicates a process-based linkage whereby microscale hydromechanical weakening (clay mineral hydration, argillization, and gypsum dissolution) is progressively manifested as macroscopic creep and acceleration in EO-derived displacement time series, with seismic preconditioning (the 2022 Ms 6.9 Menyuan earthquake) further reducing the slope’s structural threshold through mechanical fatigue, ultimately leading to slope failure under extreme precipitation. This transferable multiscale framework supports mechanism-informed hazard assessment and enables EO‑based early detection and staged early warning for clay‑rich, water‑sensitive slopes that undergo progressive creep under hydromechanical coupling, especially during extreme climatic events.

title: Single-scene thin-cloud correction for dynamic macroalgal blooms via water-referenced radiative transfer
summary: Thin clouds substantially attenuate spectral signals in satellite imagery, leading to systematic underestimation of macroalgal bloom coverage. Existing thin-cloud correction methods have critical limitations for dynamically drifting blooms: they typically require paired cloudy-clear observations or stable surface conditions, which are rarely available, or inadequately account for cloud-induced attenuation, particularly in the near-infrared band that is essential for algal quantification. This study proposes a single-scene thin-cloud correction framework for dynamic macroalgal blooms that removes both additive scattering and multiplicative attenuation from visible to NIR bands. By exploiting local atmospheric consistency between algal patches and adjacent water, the method infers localized cloud effects from neighboring water pixels. Cloud-free and cloud-affected water pixels are first identified to estimate clear-sky and cloudy top-of-atmosphere reflectance. A linear conversion model derived from radiative transfer theory then relates these two reflectances through coefficients C T and C R , whose relationship is constrained by a MODTRAN-based lookup table (LUT). The coefficients are solved by combining the conversion model with a quadratic polynomial relationship between C T and C R established from the LUT. Validation using GaoFen‑1 and Landsat‑8 imagery against near-concurrent Sentinel‑2 observations over the Southern Yellow Sea demonstrates effective near-infrared restoration. Using two complementary validation strategies—macroalgal area estimation from real images and reflectance evaluation from simulated cloudy data—the proposed method achieves consistently higher accuracy than representative state‑of‑the‑art methods. Application to golden tide events in the East China Sea further confirms its robustness and transferability. The method provides a practical, physics-guided solution for monitoring dynamic macroalgal blooms under thin-clouds contamination.

title: Satellite-based coastal monitoring through variance image composites (SatVar)
summary: The past decade has seen rapid advancements in satellite remote sensing data availability and analysis. In coastal environments, this has enabled regional to global assessments of shoreline trends, a key practical application for management and planning. However, coastal zones are inherently dynamic, while instantaneous shorelines only capture the state of the system at a particular moment in time. This study introduces a novel approach for monitoring dynamic coastal environments using satellite imagery, adapting the principle from ground-based video monitoring systems. The SatVar approach presented here uses freely available, medium resolution satellite imagery and Google Earth Engine. The method takes advantage of the increasing availability of cost-free Sentinel-2 imagery and the flexibility of collections acquired over different time periods to automatically detect highly dynamic zones through variance composites, image compositing and segmentation to obtain medium-term trends of coastal dynamics. Natural boundaries are rarely abrupt, so a zone-based (instead of a line-based) approach provides more nuanced information about transitional zones. The identified highly dynamic zones correspond to morphological processes described in literature, and are also used for shoreline extraction. This combined information can enrich understanding of coastal dynamics and overcome some of the limitations of instantaneous shorelines. The approach is tested at three locations with different morphodynamic characteristics and tidal regimes: Sancti Petri (Spain, mesotidal), Narrabeen (Australia, microtidal) and Sefton (UK, macrotidal). Potential applications to monitor changes outside the upper shoreface such as coastal dune dynamics or back-barrier environments are also discussed.

title: Robust hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits across species and spatial scales using GA-ELM
summary: Plant functional traits provide critical indicators of ecosystem functioning, biodiversity maintenance, and plant adaptive strategies under environmental change. However, hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits remains challenging because trait-related spectral signals are strongly influenced by species composition, canopy structural heterogeneity, and intertidal background effects, leading to unstable trait-spectrum relationships across species and scales. To address these limitations, this study developed a genetic algorithm-optimized extreme learning machine (GA-ELM) framework for robust retrieval of mangrove functional traits under heterogeneous mangrove spectral conditions. Three key traits, including chlorophyll content (Cab), equivalent water thickness (EWT), and leaf mass per area (LMA), were retrieved for four dominant mangrove species using leaf-level hyperspectral measurements and canopy-scale GF-5 imagery. GA-ELM generally outperformed PLSR, RF, and conventional ELM in species-specific comparisons. Leave-one-species-out validation yielded R 2 ranges of 0.61–0.75 for Cab, 0.60–0.72 for EWT, and 0.66–0.76 for LMA, indicating moderate predictive capability for previously unseen species, with performance varying among species and traits. At the canopy scale, GA-ELM achieved stable estimation accuracy for Cab, EWT, and LMA based on GF-5 imagery ( R 2 > 0.75), demonstrating that the framework can be independently calibrated for canopy-scale retrieval. Independent cross-regional validation yielded R 2 values of 0.60, 0.49, and 0.44 for Cab, EWT, and LMA, respectively, indicating moderate but reduced cross-regional transferability. Spectral sensitivity and band-selection analyses revealed species- and trait-dependent patterns that provided context for interpreting variation in predictive performance. These results remain conditional on one GF-5 acquisition per site and 30 m mixed-pixel conditions, and broader tidal-stage and cross-sensor validation is still required. These findings demonstrate the potential of GA-ELM for hyperspectral retrieval and spatial mapping of mangrove functional traits.

title: Surface-to-volume physics-informed model for 3D mesoscale eddy detection: Multi-source multi-scale fusion
summary: Mesoscale eddies play a crucial role in the ocean, and accurate detection of their three-dimensional (3D) structures is essential for understanding marine dynamics. However, 3D eddy reconstruction remains challenging: traditional methods provide limited pixel-level boundary delineation, while existing deep learning approaches suffer from insufficient physical constraints and unrealistic eddy geometries. To address this issue, we propose a surface-to-volume physics-informed model (StV-PI-EddyNet) for extracting 3D mesoscale eddies. We construct a high-quality 3D eddy dataset covering the North Pacific (100°E–100°W, 5°N–65°N) down to 1000 m for model training. The model takes sea surface height (SSH), sea surface temperature (SST), and surface current components (U/V) as inputs and consists of three core modules: 2D feature extraction, 3D feature inversion, and 3D semantic segmentation. It embeds a vorticity prediction branch for physical constraints and uses U-Net-like architectures with spatial and channel attention mechanisms. The loss function combines weighted Dice loss and a vorticity-driven physical loss (mean square error + gradient consistency loss) to ensure high segmentation accuracy and physical consistency. Experimental results show StV-PI-EddyNet model achieves 96.97% global accuracy, 84.80% weighted Dice coefficient, and 0.8955 macro-averaged F1-score. It effectively mitigates boundary distortion issues of existing methods, generating 3D eddy masks with high spatial precision. This model enjoys good scalability and can be further optimized by integrating earth observation advances in architecture design, data sources and application generalization, promoting its in-depth applications in marine and especially underwater dynamic research.

title: A method for identifying urban flood inundation based on single-temporal remote sensing imagery
summary: Rapid mapping of urban flood inundation is critical for emergency response and decision-making. However, existing methods often rely heavily on multi-temporal data or deep learning models, limiting their timeliness and computational efficiency. This study proposes an automated method for mapping urban flood inundation from a single post-event image acquired by the Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument. The method adopts a three-stage framework comprising spectral-index-based segmentation, morphological-feature-based separation, and spatial-topological assessment. It was evaluated using three flood events in Zhengzhou, China; Manville, United States; and Porto Alegre, Brazil. Independent validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.9985, 0.9371, and 0.8834; precision values of 0.6719, 0.6771, and 0.8229; and F1-scores of 0.8037, 0.7001, and 0.7615, respectively. The extracted flood extents were further compared with those obtained using two conventional approaches and were generally consistent across the three study areas. Agreement F1-scores ranged from 0.694 to 0.870 relative to pre- and post-flood change detection based on the modified normalised difference water index, and from 0.603 to 0.866 relative to newly inundated area extraction using the European Commission Joint Research Centre permanent surface-water mask. On an experimental platform equipped with an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, processing the Porto Alegre, Manville, and Zhengzhou scenes required 24.3, 2.68, and 19.8 s, respectively. These quantitative results indicate that the proposed method can identify major urban flood inundation areas under diverse geographical and hydrological conditions. Requiring only a single post-event multispectral image, no model training, and no high-performance computing, the method provides a lightweight solution for rapid urban flood inundation mapping and resource-constrained applications, including onboard satellite processing.

title: Global asymmetric mangrove-edge shifts reveal coastal squeeze under sea-level rise
summary: Changes at the land–sea interface reveal whether mangrove systems advance seaward, retreat landward, or undergo coastal squeeze as their seaward and landward boundaries converge. Yet global assessments have largely relied on area change, with less focus on these directional processes. This study applies a global coastline-normal transect framework to Global Mangrove Watch data for 1996, 2008, and 2020. By quantifying the seaward and landward edges together with width and centroid position, we distinguish expansion, directional migration, and contraction across multiple spatial scales. Globally, mangroves lost an average width of 77.2 m: the seaward edge retreated landward by 47.5 m, a pattern consistent with marine forcing including relative sea-level rise and coastal erosion, while the landward edge shifted seaward by 53.7 m, compatible with restricted accommodation space. Together, these opposing movements reveal widespread asymmetric contraction. Among regions exhibiting clear directional migration, 65.2% shifted seaward, including advances of up to 2.5 km in Marajó Bay, Brazil, whereas less frequent landward migration reached 5.6 km in the northern Gulf of Mexico. After 2008, the prevalence of landward migration increased, particularly across Asia and Africa. The edge trajectories constrain the set of plausible controls but do not uniquely attribute change to sea-level rise, sediment supply, topography, land use, or restoration. Conservation should therefore protect potential landward migration pathways while accounting for uncertainty in the mechanisms producing individual local trajectories.

title: Multi-task learning for simultaneous surface water and burned area mapping from earth observation data
summary: Multi-task learning has emerged as a promising approach for combining related tasks into a unified framework with reduced computational costs through shared representations. However, its application to hazard mapping using Earth Observation data remains underexplored. In this study, we provide the first systematic evaluation of multi-task deep learning architectures for simultaneous detection of crisis information (surface water and burned area) using Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 optical imagerytwo societally critical hazards with strong operational demand for rapid and accurate detection. We evaluate five semantic segmentation architectures: three U-Net variants with different encoders (MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B4, ResNet50) and two transformer-based SegFormer models (SegFormer-B0, SegFormer-B4). Each architecture was trained in both single-task learning and multi-task learning modes. For reference data, we employed the benchmark S1S2-Water dataset for water body detection and constructed a novel burned area dataset by integrating diverse global datasets with already available in-house annotations. Both reference datasets cover heterogeneous geographic regions and temporal periods. The results show that multi-task learning effectiveness is highly architecture-dependent. Burned area detection achieved F1-scores ranging from 0.624 to 0.701, with three of five architectures showing improvements under multi-task learning. SegFormer-B4 reached the best performance (F1-score: 0.67) with gains of +8.24% over its single-task baseline, while EfficientNet-B4 achieved the highest absolute accuracy (F1-score: 0.701). Conversely, ResNet50 exhibited negative transfer with an F1-score decrease of 8.24%, demonstrating that not all architectures benefit from multi-task learning. Water detection performance remained consistently high across all models (F1-score > 0.97), with SegFormer-B4 achieving an F1-score of 0.98. Importantly, the multi-task framework reduces inference time by 89–91% and parameter count by 17–48% compared to maintaining two separate single-task models, demonstrating its practical value for operational emergency mapping services where rapid hazard assessment is critical.

title: Hydroclimatic signatures of flash drought heterogeneity and rice-yield responses in China
summary: Flash drought poses a growing threat to agricultural production because its rapid onset limits timely monitoring and adaptive management. Using ERA5-Land root-zone soil moisture, this study identified flash drought events across China from 2004 to 2023, characterized their spatiotemporal patterns and hydroclimatic associations, assessed cross-product consistency of the identified onset signals, and examined their associations with rice-yield anomalies. GLEAM root-zone soil moisture was used for cross-product onset-consistency assessment, and a spatially validated Random Forest–GeoShapley framework was applied to examine the hydroclimatic associations of flash drought duration, severity, and intensity. Flash droughts occurred more frequently in southern and southwestern China, whereas longer and more severe events were concentrated in northern arid, plateau, and high-latitude regions. GLEAM showed consistent root-zone soil-moisture depletion around ERA5-Land-identified onset dates, supporting the timing and direction of the identified onset signals. GeoShapley analysis indicated that geographic background accounted for a substantial share of the total contribution. Precipitation deficit contributed most strongly to duration and severity, whereas intensity showed a more distributed contribution from precipitation deficit and atmospheric-demand variables. April–September drought exposure was generally associated with lower rice-yield anomalies, with flash drought showing more negative exposure–response estimates than slow drought, particularly in the Northeast China Plain. These findings clarify attribute-specific hydroclimatic associations of flash drought and support region-specific monitoring and rice-production risk assessment in China.

title: Stage-integrated fire resilience assessment of forest vegetation and its driving factors
summary: Forest vegetation responses to fire intensities remain insufficiently understood, particularly across the successive stages of resistance and post-fire recovery. To address this issue, we selected 771 independent fire events that occurred between 2005 and 2020 in representative conifer-dominated forests of Northeast China, including larch-, pine-, and spruce-dominated vegetation communities. The fire month was defined as the disturbance onset, and each fire event was examined over a 97-month observation period comprising 48 months before and 48 months after the fire. Forest fires were classified into normal- and high-intensity groups, and a three-stage analytical framework was developed to link pre-fire vegetation health, resistance during fire disturbance, and post-fire recovery. Using historical burned-area records and a Transformer-based counterfactual model, we reconstructed fire-free trajectories of the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), and Net Primary Productivity (NPP). These indicators were subsequently integrated through tensor decomposition to construct a Composite Resilience Index (CRI). Because these air and soil temperatures were naturally varying environmental factors rather than experimentally controlled variables, their effects were statistically accounted for as time-varying covariates in the modeling and driver-attribution analyses. Cumulative resistance was consistently higher than instantaneous resistance, indicating that vegetation partially compensated for its initial fire-induced losses over time. NPP exhibited the greatest short-term stability, whereas SIF showed the strongest immediate sensitivity to fire disturbance. Under high-intensity fire, the fitted recovery-deviation transition points occurred at 9.5 months for EVI, 10.5 months for SIF, and 36.5 months for NPP. These values indicate that the recovery trajectory of ecosystem productivity changed substantially later than those of vegetation structure and photosynthetic functioning. The CRI was significantly lower at 12, 24, and 48 months following high-intensity fire, indicating a persistent multidimensional resilience deficit rather than a short-lived reduction immediately after the fire. SHAP analysis further identified monthly air and soil temperatures as the dominant environmental predictors of post-fire resilience. These findings provide a multidimensional basis for forest fire-risk assessment, vegetation vulnerability evaluation, and stage-specific restoration management in high-latitude forest ecosystems.

title: Spaceborne multi-sensor tracking reveals hydrologic decoupling during the record-breaking Sahara flood
summary: Satellite remote sensing enables large-scale quantification of extreme hydrologic events in data-scarce regions, yet the integration of multi-sensor observations to resolve hydrologic responses remains limited. The record-breaking 2024 Sahara flood presents a unique opportunity to evaluate satellite-based characterisation of hydrologic extremes in hyper-arid environments. By integrating multi-sensor satellite observations of precipitation, surface inundation, and terrestrial water storage, we provide a comprehensive assessment of this event’s hydrologic scope. Intense rainfall, delivering annual precipitation totals within just a few days, triggered widespread flooding, with the 2024 inundation extent estimated to show an approximate cross-sensor increase of 38 ± 9% relative to the historical GLAD/Landsat benchmark (1999–2023), reaching up to a 40-fold increase in some basins. Concurrently, regional terrestrial water storage exhibited an unprecedented surge, with its intra-annual amplitude doubling the long-term average. However, this hydrologic response was spatially variable. In the eastern basins, surface inundation and terrestrial water storage increased concurrently, indicating strong hydrologic coupling. In contrast, several western basins exhibited pronounced surface flooding but comparatively weak TWS responses, revealing a decoupling between flood magnitude and basin-scale storage response. These findings highlight the capability of multi-sensor satellite observations to resolve spatially heterogeneous hydrologic responses and reveal the non-stationarity in the conversion of flood hazards into terrestrial water storage gains in hyper-arid environments. This study provides a transferable approach for monitoring hydrologic extremes in ungauged regions.

title: Improved estimation of lake storage variation via DEM reconstruction integrating elevation and morphological constraints
summary: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. However, most existing methods primarily rely on elevation-matched contours and discard those without elevation data. Consequently, the loss of morphological constraints leads to incorrect topographic structures and significantly amplifies reconstruction errors where elevation data are sparse. To overcome this limitation, we proposed a valued and Non-valued contour–based Unified DEM reconstruction model (NUDEM), which integrates contours with elevations and those without elevations to exploit both elevation constraints and morphological constraints. Evaluated on four lakes in the Tibetan Plateau, NUDEM consistently outperformed five existing methods in DEM reconstruction, reducing the RMSE by approximately 60% compared to the second-best method, with an average RMSE of 0.93 m and a minimum RMSE of 0.15 m. For lake storage variation estimation, NUDEM improved R2 by about 30% over other DEM-based methods and nearly doubled the R2 of traditional hypsometric-curve-based methods. This method provides a low-cost, remote sensing-based solution for large-scale lake DEM reconstruction, offering significant potential for improving the accuracy of lake storage variation estimation.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
summary: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. However, systematic quantitative assessments of vegetation responses and their drivers under such compound extremes remain limited. Using meteorological and remote sensing data, we identified growing-season CDHW events across Central Asia from 1982 to 2023. Integrating the Kernel normalized difference vegetation index (KNDVI) and the long-term continuous SIF-informed photosynthesis proxy (LCSPP), we established a vegetation response indicator system including total loss (LOSStot), maximum decline (DECmax), and time to decline (TIMEdec) to characterize vegetation damage. We further applied the XGBoost model and SHAP analysis to quantify the environmental driving effects and interactions. The results indicate that CDHW events increased significantly during 1982–2023, with heatwave frequency rising at 0.38 days yr−1 and an abrupt shift around 1996. High-frequency CDHW events were primarily concentrated in north-central Kazakhstan and northern Xinjiang, China, while their frequency and duration generally increased with latitude, indicating a pronounced northward enhancement pattern. CDHW caused larger vegetation losses than individual drought or heatwave events. Event duration was the most important environmental variable of LOSStot, with the highest mean SHAP value (0.140), while precipitation anomalies during events showed a strong association with rapid vegetation decline, with a direct path coefficient of 0.333 for DECmax. This study clarifies vegetation loss characteristics and key contributing factors under compound extremes in Central Asia, providing a scientific basis for ecological risk assessment and climate adaptation in arid regions.
